status: CANDIDATE — not issued, not scored, not referenced by any scenario record, not in the dashboard path. The issued v2 records (2026-10-15) are untouched.
description: Illustrative scenario endpoints for the forward production question the shipping evidence raises about the issued v2 standoff path ('no net Gulf recovery', world production flat at the September reported 101.30 mb/d through 2026). The same-definition Kpler regional measure recovered from -28% (Oct 14 edition) to -19% (Oct 19 edition, 19,041 kbd 7-day avg vs ~23,306 baseline) with the East-West bypass at ~5.8 mbd; a syndicated print (Bloomberg, Oct 20) claims total Middle East oil flows of 24.0M b/d for week e/Oct 18 — above the prewar 23.3M — but is unreconciled (no definition/window). The endpoints: (a) A = issued v2 standoff (unchanged); (b) B = the month-by-month midpoint between the two issued world-production levels at identical consumption (monthly gap halved — a point on the existing sensitivity line, NOT a measured Gulf recovery rate and NOT a barrels-exported-to-production conversion); (c) C = the EIA baseline (v2 corridor-holds, adjustment 0). The endpoints are scenarios, not physical bounds: no supported interval for the eventual outcome is asserted.

scenarios.name: No net Gulf recovery (issued v2 standoff — endpoint A)
scenarios.definition: The issued v2 standoff path, unchanged: world production flat at the September reported level through 2026, non-Gulf growth only across 2027.
scenarios.status: reference to the issued v2 standoff (site/src/data/world-stocks-assumptions-v2026-10-15.json) — not modified

scenarios.name: Month-by-month midpoint between the two issued world-production levels (endpoint B — ILLUSTRATION)
scenarios.definition: The month-by-month midpoint between the two issued world-production levels (standoff and EIA baseline), at identical consumption: monthly production adjustment = half the issued standoff adjustment (the corridor-holds adjustment is 0, so this is the midpoint of the monthly gap). This is a point on the existing sensitivity line — a midpoint of TWO WORLD PRODUCTION LEVELS, not a measured 'half-rate Gulf recovery'; there is no Gulf/non-Gulf decomposition here, and shipment recovery does not identify world production, inventories, domestic use or a 2027 recovery rate.
assumptions: (illustrative, stated not calibrated) the Kpler regional 7-day avg holds at or above 19 mb/d in the next two briefings (the -19% reading does not deteriorate)
(illustrative, stated not calibrated) the East-West bypass holds at or above ~5.8 mbd (no new confirmed damage; the Red Sea leg not closed)
(illustrative, stated not calibrated) no confirmed production damage at Ghawar/Abqaiq/Shedgum or the Eastern Province complex

no assumption is made about where the preliminary prints will settle: the briefing's 'typically settled 1.5-2x' is Kpler's statement about the Kpler series, recorded as provenance and NOT used to position this midpoint
scenarios.uncertainty: An illustration, not an interval: the three endpoints are scenarios (two of them references to issued paths), not physical bounds, and no supported interval for the eventual outcome is asserted. The shipping evidence is directional only — regional recovery (-28% -> -19%) and the bypass flows argue against 'no net recovery', while the strait measure (-54%) and the attack rate (18 vessels in 2 weeks) argue against 'full recovery' — and exports are not world production (consumption, stock draws and on-water effects sit in between).

scenarios.name: Full EIA baseline recovery (endpoint C)
scenarios.definition: The EIA STEO Oct 6 baseline itself (the v2 corridor-holds path, adjustment 0).
scenarios.status: reference to the issued v2 corridor-holds path — not modified

illustrative_reexamination_condition.status: ILLUSTRATION, not an automatic promotion: this artifact does not promote the issued v2 path on its own, and no code or condition issues a new forecast from it.
illustrative_reexamination_condition.condition: (illustrative) two consecutive Kpler briefings with the regional 7-day avg at or above 19 mb/d (data dates at least 7 days apart) AND a comparable-basis confirmation of the 'total Middle East flows at/above prewar' print (definition + window printed).
illustrative_reexamination_condition.if_met: It would argue for re-examining the storage path. Issuing a new dated scenario version (regen-scenarios.py --emit-records) requires an explicit, dated human decision logged in the pass log — the v2026-10-15 records stay frozen and authoritative until then, and the published dashboard is unchanged meanwhile.
illustrative_reexamination_condition.moot_condition: Confirmed production damage at a named Gulf field/terminal makes the corridor-holds premise of the EIA baseline itself questionable, so endpoint C (and this illustration built on it) is no longer a sensible reference: the issued v2 standoff path stands as published, and the question becomes the damage itself (the damage would be assessed on its own merits — it does not by itself restore any prior fixed production level).
